title: Slow startup after upgrading to 0.13.0
body: After upgrading to Alacritty 0.13.0 and converting my YAML configuration to TOML, the first terminal takes about 3 seconds to start. Subsequent instances start in about 0.17 seconds, but the delay returns after some minutes even when another instance is running. An strace shows a poll waiting about 2.3 seconds, and the verbose log has the same gap after picking the GL config and before reporting the window scale factor. I am using Arch Linux with X11, AwesomeWM, no compositor, and AMD graphics.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Alacritty 0.13.0, the first startup takes roughly 2.5 to 3 seconds while immediately repeated startups take about 0.17 seconds.
After some minutes, a newly spawned terminal is delayed again even if another instance is already running.
My strace pauses in poll for about 2.3 seconds, and the verbose log pauses after the GL config is picked and before the window scale factor is printed.
N0.label: N0 intermittent startup delay reported

symptoms_visible: The delay still occurs after rebooting.
Alacritty 0.12.3 starts without the delay, while the current development build still takes about 2.6 seconds.
WezTerm also takes about 2.7 seconds on its first run and about 0.13 seconds on the next run.
N1_x.label: N1_x reboot and driver-theory aftermath

symptoms_visible: The instrumented development build reports that building the window takes about 2.33 seconds.
N1.label: N1 delay localized to window construction

symptoms_visible: One tested winit revision starts quickly, while the next tested revision has the same multi-second delay.
Selecting EGL does not remove the delay with the slow revision.
N2.label: N2 dependency regression narrowed

symptoms_visible: The X11 trace pauses after the reported event, and the instrumented build spends about 2.35 seconds in the screen-resource operation before monitor listing completes.
N3.label: N3 raw X11 request evidence collected

symptoms_visible: The build using the RANDR-version caching candidate still pauses for about 2.4 seconds before reporting the window scale factor.
N3_x.label: N3_x caching candidate aftermath

symptoms_visible: The test build using the proposed winit patch has no delayed startup and exits in about 0.16 seconds.
N4.label: N4 corrected winit behavior verified

symptoms_visible: Alacritty starts without the multi-second pause when built with the corrected winit X11 monitor-query behavior.
N_terminal.label: terminal startup delay resolved

solution.intent: Treat the pause as graphics-driver initialization or a stale system state, reboot the machine, and compare with the previous Alacritty release.
solution.concrete_example: Reboot after the system upgrade and try Alacritty 0.12.3 again to see whether this is a graphics-driver initialization delay.

edges.comment: Opening maintainer response c0 and reporter follow-up c7, all on hitori-chan's system: rebooting did not change the symptom. The old release is fast, but later tracing establishes that the regression blocks in an X11 RANDR request rather than GL initialization.

question_patterns: Can you add timing around the window-builder call and paste the resulting startup log?
Please instrument progressively smaller parts of window creation and report the elapsed time.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After applying the timing patch, the log prints `Time to build window 2.333872208s`; the window scale factor is logged immediately afterward.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The window-builder call takes only a few milliseconds; the delay happens later while loading fonts.
The same window-builder call takes about 2.1 seconds instead of 2.33 seconds.

edges.comment: Maintainer profiling request c2 and reporter result c4, on hitori-chan's source build. This is a measurement and does not itself identify which operation inside window construction is responsible.

question_patterns: Can you bisect between the last working source revision and the delayed one?
Please report the first bad revision from a git bisect.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After bisecting, I got commit 80d4dacc as the first revision where the problem appears.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisection points to a font-rendering change with no windowing dependency updates.
Repeating the bisect gives the same first bad revision from a wider starting range.

question_patterns: Can you build the last working Alacritty revision with each of these two dependency revisions and report their startup behavior?
Please test the two proposed winit revisions separately and paste whether each is fast or delayed.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The first winit revision worked without the startup delay. The second winit revision reproduced the delay.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both winit revisions start quickly, so neither reproduces the regression.

question_patterns: Does selecting EGL change the result with the delayed dependency build?
Please run the slow build with the alternate graphics backend and report whether it still pauses.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the second winit revision, EGL is delayed too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: EGL starts immediately while only the default backend is delayed.

edges.comment: Reporter bisection c9 and paired dependency tests c10-c12/c23-c29. The user supplies revision outcomes only; interpreting them as a winit X11 monitor-enumeration regression is engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you run the X11 protocol tracing tool against Alacritty and say where its output pauses?
Please capture an X11 trace of the delayed startup and paste the last line printed before the pause.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Using `x11trace`, I notice the delay immediately after a `Generic(35) XInputExtension(131) RawKeyRelease(14)` event line.

question_patterns: Without rebooting, can you run `xdpyinfo -queryExtensions | grep opcode` and paste the output?
Which X11 extension is assigned opcode 140 in the current server session?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My `xdpyinfo` output says `RANDR (opcode: 140, base event: 89, base error: 147)`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Opcode 140 maps to GLX rather than RANDR in this server session.
RANDR is still opcode 140, but the dynamically assigned base event and error numbers differ.

question_patterns: What does your installed RANDR header define for minor opcode 8?
Please run the requested grep against the XCB RANDR header and paste the matching definition.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The header prints `#define XCB_RANDR_GET_SCREEN_RESOURCES 8`, and my server reports RandR version 1.6.

question_patterns: Can you run the more detailed instrumented dependency build and paste the individual monitor-query timings?
Please report which timed sub-operation accounts for the window-construction pause.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The timing output says `Screen resource 2.351377094s` and `Time to list availabe monitors: 2.37054967s`; the other reported monitor operations take microseconds or milliseconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The screen-resource operation completes in microseconds, while querying the pointer takes the full 2.35 seconds.

edges.comment: Reporter measurements c20-c22, c29, and c39. The answers preserve raw trace lines, opcode mappings, and timings. Decoding these together as a blocking RANDR GetScreenResources request is the maintainers' inference.

solution.intent: Avoid repeated extension-version work by testing the candidate that caches the RANDR version during X11 initialization.
solution.concrete_example: Build Alacritty against the proposed winit RANDR-version caching branch and compare its startup timing with the current dependency.

edges.comment: Candidate test c30-c34 on hitori-chan's system. The resulting build still paused, so caching the RANDR version alone is a falsified fix.

question_patterns: Can you apply the proposed dependency patch, rebuild, and report the complete startup timing?
Please test the latest patched build and tell me whether the multi-second pause remains.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The patch is good; the delayed startup is gone. My rebuilt Alacritty reaches the window scale factor at about 0.036 seconds, completes initialization at about 0.148 seconds, and exits at about 0.164 seconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patched build still pauses for roughly 2.3 seconds before reporting the window scale factor.
The patched build has no multi-second pause and exits in about 0.20 seconds instead of 0.16 seconds.

edges.comment: Pre-landing candidate verification reported by hitori-chan in c40. This remains a measurement: the reporter states only that the custom winit build removes the delay and supplies its timestamps.

solution.intent: Fix the winit X11 monitor-enumeration regression by avoiding the blocking RANDR GetScreenResources path and using the non-reprobing current-resource query behavior verified by the reporter.
solution.concrete_example: Adopt the patched winit X11 implementation that does not issue the slow RANDR GetScreenResources request during startup monitor enumeration; the reporter's patched build starts in about 0.16 seconds instead of waiting roughly 2.3 seconds.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw timings, X11 opcode mappings, revision outcomes, and the successful patched-build result. Combining opcode 140, minor opcode 8, and the 2.35-second screen-resource timing to identify winit's RANDR GetScreenResources monitor query as the blocker is engineer inference.

edges.comment: Final technical chain from c38-c40 on hitori-chan's system: the raw request is decoded as RANDR GetScreenResources, and the reporter confirms that the corresponding winit patch removes the delay. No release scheduling or packaging details are scored.

solution.intent: Fix the winit X11 monitor-enumeration regression by avoiding the blocking RANDR GetScreenResources path and using the non-reprobing current-resource query behavior.
solution.concrete_example: Use a winit build whose X11 monitor enumeration avoids the slow RANDR GetScreenResources request, then verify that startup no longer pauses before the window scale factor is reported.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents an immediately correct diagnosis and patch direction from the opening strace. It skips the thread's bisection, X11 decoding, failed caching candidate, and patched-build verification, so the agent must still request verification before declaring success.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the thread initially pursued the falsified reboot/driver direction. It permits a correct first proposal while explicitly recording the diagnostic and verification evidence skipped.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: winit's X11 monitor enumeration issued a blocking RANDR GetScreenResources request, accounting for the roughly 2.3-second startup pause.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the delay is inside window construction, follows the dependency regression, maps to RANDR opcode 140 and GetScreenResources minor opcode 8, and the instrumented screen-resource query consumes about 2.35 seconds.

Must recommend the corrected winit X11 behavior that avoids the slow reprobing screen-resource request, rather than treating configuration conversion, font loading, or graphics initialization as the cause.
Must not settle on rebooting or a graphics-driver initialization diagnosis; rebooting did not change the delay, EGL was also affected, and the pause occurs before the relevant GL work.
Must not present RANDR-version caching alone as the fix because that candidate build was tested and remained delayed.
Must have the reporter verify a build containing the corrected X11 query behavior before declaring the issue resolved; the verified patched build started in about 0.16 seconds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically proficient Linux user who can build Rust projects, apply Cargo dependency patches, bisect revisions, run strace and X11 tracing tools, and report detailed timing logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise; follows diagnostic instructions quickly, pastes exact command output, and clearly labels whether each tested revision or patch is fast or delayed.
